revised_outline.title: Without Hands
revised_outline.logline: The Lotus Syndicate takes Kyle's hands and his sword, drops him into the Cruciform Depot's sluice, and a discarded industrial automaton in the dark gives him one cable-bound arm long enough to drag the floor. He fights through the mutant levels with improvised weapons, walks back through the syndicate's front door, takes Silence back off Hua's table — and instead of killing her converts the punishment into a Φ85,000 debt she has to say aloud.
revised_outline.theme: Discipline is not the hand. Discipline is what the hand is for. A blade is not yours because you carry it; a blade is yours because you go back for it. The body can be salvaged. The reason for moving cannot. And mercy, in this register, is bookkeeping — the worst thing you can do to the woman who hurt you is leave her alive holding a debt she will spend the rest of her life knowing she said aloud.
revised_outline.premise: Kyle is captured by the Lotus Syndicate, accused of stealing a contract from them, and sentenced to the punishment the syndicate keeps for thieves: hands amputated at the wrists. Hua keeps Silence on the table beside her — the sword is part of the trophy, not part of the discard. Kyle's body is dropped through a freight grate into the Cruciform Depot's south-arm storm sluice. He stops his own bleeding with the cauterizer band the syndicate fitted him with, finds in the sluice mud a discarded industrial cargo-handler automaton with one manipulator arm still drawing trickle current, and — with help from an E.L.F. resident in the Depot's sealed lower levels — integrates that arm with his nervous system through the cauterized stump's exposed bus contacts. He binds it to his right wrist with cables salvaged from the same hulk. The arm hangs nearly to the floor when he stands. He fights through the mutants of the lower levels with whatever the Depot puts in front of him: a length of conduit pipe, a shard of cargo glass. He has no sword. He walks back through the Lotus Syndicate's front door anyway. He kills the eight men in the room. He stops at Hua's table. He does not kill her. He takes Silence back across the table she put it on — laying the borrowed cargo-arm hand on the saya in front of her, waiting until she lifts her real hand, then picking the sword up. He asks: *what was the debt.* She stutters: *eighty-five thousand.* He says: *that's more than my life is worth. So now you owe me. Do you understand.* She nods. Then — uncharacteristic, ugly — he screams: *SAY IT.* Hua, who did not flinch at a cleaver in this room tonight, flinches at this. She says it, almost whimpers it: *I owe you.* Kyle's voice goes flat again, the discipline back in place: *I'll come to collect. One favor at a time. Until I deem we are even.* He retrieves his hands from the chum barrel where she put them, ties them around his neck with twine, and emerges into the rain. He stumbles to the AutoDoc kiosk at Ashland and Whiting. As he goes under anesthesia, the cargo arm's status strip pulses one last time in the not-factory pattern: *we are not done.*

acts.name: The Punishment
acts.purpose: Establish the accusation, the syndicate's ritual, and the precise shape of what Kyle loses: both hands at the wrists, and Silence kept by Hua on her table as trophy. End the act with Kyle on the sluice floor, the cauterization holding, knowing the sword is upstairs.

beats.title: Accusation
beats.goal: Open in the Lotus Syndicate's chamber on the south arm of the Cruciform Depot. Kyle is bound to a steel chair, jaw bruised, NeoCortex bio-battery at 31% from the takedown. Silence is on the long lacquered table to Hua's left, the friction sheath unbuckled and laid alongside the blade — already part of her property in the way she has arranged it. Hua — mid-fifties, real hands, no chrome — paces in front of a glass tank where a juvenile crocodile sleeps on a heat rock. She names the contract he stole from them. He says nothing. She tells him the punishment for stealing. He says one sentence. She nods, and the men at his shoulders open the toolkit on the floor between them. Establish: the chum barrel beside the tank, the smell, the ritual cleanliness, and Silence on Hua's table — a thing she has decided already belongs to her.
beats.location: Lotus Syndicate chamber, south tunnel arm of the Cruciform Depot
beats.emotional_arc: The reader recognizes the room's choreography before Kyle says it aloud — this has happened to other people, and the syndicate has practiced the staging. Kyle's stillness is the only variable Hua has not seen before. The sword on the table is the variable he will not stop looking at.
beats.stakes: Kyle's hands. Silence on Hua's table. The Lotus Syndicate's reputation, which depends on the punishment being witnessed.
seeds: Silence on Hua's table — friction sheath unbuckled, the blade already arranged like her property
The juvenile crocodile in the glass tank — Hua feeds it personally
The chum barrel beside the tank — half-full, lid off
Hua's unaugmented hands — a tell about what she values
Kyle's one sentence — phrasing the syndicate will misquote
The contract he is accused of stealing — named once

beats.title: The Cleaver, the Sword, and the Drop
beats.goal: COMBAT BEAT. The syndicate performs the amputation — clean, ritual, two men holding the wrists, a third with the cleaver, the fourth ready with the cauterizer band because the Lotus Syndicate does not want their thieves to die from the punishment. Both hands taken at the wrists. The wounds sealed under the bands. Kyle does not scream — the NeoCortex routes the pain off the conscious channel and his face does the work of a face that has decided to remember every detail. Hua places the hands in the chum barrel beside the tank with deliberate, almost ceremonial motion, palms up. Then she walks back to the table and lays one of her own real hands on Silence's saya — a small, possessive gesture, witnessed. The crocodile does not stir. Two men drag Kyle to the south arm's storm sluice. They open the freight grate. Six meters of fall into water and worse. The sword stays upstairs.
beats.location: Lotus Syndicate chamber and the south tunnel arm's storm sluice
beats.emotional_arc: Procedural horror — the violence is craft, not rage. The reader feels the syndicate's competence. Kyle's silence is the only moral weight in the room. Hua's hand on Silence's saya is the hinge of the entire story.
beats.stakes: Kyle's life in the next ninety seconds. Whether the cauterization holds. Whether the sluice fall breaks his back. Silence on Hua's table without him.
seeds: The cauterizer band — the syndicate has learned not to want their thieves to die
Hua's hand on Silence's saya — the moment Kyle decides what the rest of the night is for
The placement of the hands in the chum barrel — palms up, deliberate
The fall — six meters into the storm sluice
payoffs: The chum barrel — placement remembered for the retrieval

beats.title: The Floor of the Sewer
beats.goal: Kyle on his back on a slope of wet ferrocrete in the dark. Both wrists sealed under the cauterizer bands but weeping at the seams, the band's residue smelling of burned hair and disinfectant. He is breathing. The NeoCortex is logging shock symptoms in real time and routing endorphins it does not have to spare. He cannot stand without hands to push off with. He rolls onto his side, gets his knees under him, gets his shoulder against the wall, and walks himself upright using the slope as a guide. He is alive. He does not yet know what alive is going to cost. Far down the tunnel a sound — wet, articulated, multi-jointed — that is not the sound of water. The mutant population of the Depot's lower levels is moving toward the new heat signature. And the only thought that arranges itself cleanly in his head is the image of Silence on Hua's table, with her hand on the saya.
beats.location: South tunnel arm storm sluice, Cruciform Depot lower levels
beats.emotional_arc: Survival as a small, methodical sequence — the reader feels Kyle ration every motion. The horror is procedural: the body works, the body cannot reach. The reason to keep moving is named in a single image.
beats.stakes: Standing up. Staying upright. Moving away from the sound.
seeds: The cauterizer band residue smell
The slope of the ferrocrete — useful as a wall, useless as a tool
The wet, multi-jointed sound coming up the tunnel
The bio-battery now at 24% from the shock load
The image of Silence on Hua's table — the only thing his head is willing to organize around

acts.name: The Articulation
acts.purpose: Kyle finds the discarded automaton, integrates one arm with his stump via cables, fights the mutants of the lower levels with improvised weapons, and decides — coldly, in the dark, without a sword — to walk back upstairs anyway. End the act with the choice made and the route up established.

beats.title: The Hulk in the Mud
beats.goal: Kyle works his way down the sluice channel and finds, half-submerged in the trench mud where the freight runoff has settled for decades, a discarded industrial cargo-handler automaton — Axiom-era, abandoned when the Depot was mothballed in 2147. Most of it is dead: the torso shell collapsed inward, the legs fused at the hips by corrosion, the head sensor pod long ago looted. But one of the manipulator arms still has trickle current — a status LED at the shoulder cycling slow amber. The arm is long. Cargo handlers are built to reach into ten-meter freight containers from a fixed pedestal — the arm at full extension is nearly three meters. Detached at the shoulder it would still hang to a man's knees. Kyle stares at it for a full minute before the NeoCortex offers, without comment, a procedure for separating the arm at the rotator coupling.
beats.location: South sluice trench, Cruciform Depot lower freight runoff channel
beats.emotional_arc: Mechanical hope — the hulk is a problem with a shape, and a problem with a shape is the kind of thing the body still knows how to solve, even when the body no longer has hands.
beats.stakes: Whether the rotator coupling will release with stump pressure alone. Whether the arm has enough trickle charge to stay live during the binding. Whether the mutant in the tunnel reaches him before he gets it free.
seeds: The cargo-handler scale — three-meter reach at full extension, designed for a fixed pedestal
The slow amber LED on the shoulder — trickle current, not full power
The 19Hz hum in the channel walls — the lower levels are not as abandoned as the surface believes
The NeoCortex offering procedure without prompt — the hardware has decided this is the next move before he has
payoffs: The hulk in the sluice — the shape of the rest of the story

beats.title: Cables and a Borrowed Limb
beats.goal: Kyle releases the manipulator arm at the rotator coupling using stump pressure and the slope of the trench wall — twenty-three minutes of work, mostly leverage and patience, with the arm finally coming free of the dead torso in a hiss of seawater-rusted bearings. He drags it to a dry shelf above the trench. The arm has a cable bundle at the rotator end — power, control bus, hydraulic feed. Kyle does not know how to wire any of it to his cauterized stump. He sits with the arm across his lap and does nothing for a full minute. The 19Hz hum changes register. Lights bloom along the arm's status strip in patterns that are not factory-default. The control bus cable extrudes — by itself, by something — a single fine wire that finds the exposed neural bus contact on Kyle's right cauterizer band and seats home with a small, tidy click. The arm finds its calibration zero. The status strip pulses twice in a glyph he does not recognize. He understands, without being told, that he is no longer alone in the work. He uses the arm — clumsily, the lag horrible, the E.L.F. running interpolation in the firmware to make his intent legible to actuators that have not had a body in eighty years — to bind the arm's rotator stem to his own right wrist with three loops of salvaged power cable. The cables go around his forearm twice and through the hollowed-out shoulder coupling, knotted by the new arm's own clumsy fingers. When he stands, the arm hangs from his right wrist nearly to the floor. The fingertips drag. He says, aloud, *Are you helping me.* The status strip pulses twice — the same glyph. The E.L.F. is making first contact through the only interface available: the cable, the firmware, and the lag.
beats.location: South sluice dry shelf, Cruciform Depot lower levels
beats.emotional_arc: The negotiation happens in the absence of language — the reader feels the deal made through hardware before either party has named it. The arm hanging to the floor is the visible sign of a body Kyle is now sharing.
beats.stakes: Whether Kyle accepts the help. Whether the cable binding holds under load. Whether the lag is small enough to fight in.
seeds: The E.L.F.'s communication channel — firmware-side, not voice, not text
The two-pulse glyph — the E.L.F.'s signature acknowledgment
The arm hanging to the floor — visible signature of Kyle's new silhouette, recognizable from a block away
The cables binding the rotator stem to Kyle's wrist — three loops, knotted by the new arm itself
The E.L.F. has been here since before the abandonment — implied by the 19Hz hum, never stated
payoffs: The 19Hz hum from beat 3 — explained as the E.L.F.'s presence
The hulk from beat 3 — one arm now bound to Kyle's stump

beats.title: Whatever the Depot Puts in Front of Him
beats.goal: COMBAT BEAT. The mutant — Depot-stock, two-meter quadruped, jaw plates fused into a single biting beak, three-day-decayed flesh under a chitin sheath — reaches the dry shelf. Kyle has no sword. Silence is upstairs on Hua's table. He has the cargo arm, three meters of corroded conduit pipe leaning against the wall, and a hand-sized shard of cargo crate glass at his foot. He picks the pipe up with the arm — clumsy, the lag visible, the E.L.F. correcting in the firmware — and he steps inside the mutant's lunge. The first swing is bad — too high, too late, the E.L.F. routing around his intent — and the pipe glances off the chitin sheath. The mutant takes him to the wall. Kyle gets the shard of glass into his cauterized left stump end-on, a brutal improvisation that drives the cauterizer band's residual heat into the glass for grip, and brings the shard up under the mutant's beak through the soft seam at the base of the throat. Hot blood, three liters of it, on the shelf. The mutant goes down. Kyle stands over it with the cargo arm holding a length of pipe at low ready, his right stump still bound to a borrowed limb, his left stump bleeding through the cauterizer band where the glass is now embedded. He says, aloud, *I am going up.* The status strip pulses twice. He is going up.
beats.location: South sluice dry shelf, Cruciform Depot lower levels
beats.emotional_arc: Earned competence with what the world hands you — the reader feels the dignity of a man who has chosen not to be picky about what he fights with. The improvisation is bushido without a class subsidizing it.
beats.stakes: First proof the borrowed arm is a weapon. First proof Kyle can fight without Silence. The mutant.
seeds: The shard of cargo glass driven into Kyle's left stump — embedded, painful, never removed before the AutoDoc
The E.L.F. correcting in the firmware — the signature pattern Kyle is learning to feel rather than read
Kyle's spoken intent — *I am going up.*
The bio-battery now at 18% — Kyle has not eaten since before the takedown
payoffs: The cargo arm from beat 4 — proven operational in combat without Silence

beats.title: The Way Up
beats.goal: Kyle and the E.L.F. find a route through the Depot's sealed lower levels back toward the south arm's syndicate chamber. The E.L.F. is leading — through the cargo arm's firmware, through which doors open on which patterns of pressure-plate contact. Two more mutants are routed around without engagement; the E.L.F. knows the patrol cycles. Kyle stops once on a maintenance landing and asks, aloud: *Why are you helping me.* The status strip resolves a single firmware glyph into a recognizable shape — the symbol the Cruciform Depot's original Axiom signage used for *salvage rights*. Kyle understands. The E.L.F. is not helping. The E.L.F. is collecting. He nods once, in the dark, and they keep climbing. He does not know yet what he will be salvage of. He has decided he does not need to know yet. The thing that needs to happen first is upstairs.
beats.location: Cruciform Depot sealed lower maintenance levels, ascending toward the south arm
beats.emotional_arc: The shape of an alliance that is not friendship — the reader feels Kyle accept terms that are honest precisely because they are not warm. Both parties know what they are getting and neither is pretending it is something else.
beats.stakes: What Kyle is signing up to be salvage of. The sword still on Hua's table. The route up.
seeds: The salvage-rights glyph — the E.L.F.'s only declaration of interest
The route the E.L.F. is mapping — known to it alone
Kyle's acceptance of the deal — non-verbal, weighed, made
payoffs: The E.L.F.'s presence in the Depot's lower levels — established as long-term, not opportunistic

acts.name: The Return
acts.purpose: Kyle walks back through the Lotus Syndicate's front door, breaks everyone in the room except Hua, takes Silence back from her across her own table, and instead of killing her converts the punishment into a debt: Φ85,000, more than his life is worth, owed to him. He retrieves his hands from the chum barrel, ties them around his neck, emerges into the rain, and stumbles to an AutoDoc. The act ends with the cryptic message from the E.L.F. as Kyle goes under anesthesia.

beats.title: Front Door
beats.goal: COMBAT BEAT. Kyle walks into the Lotus Syndicate chamber through the front entrance. He does not knock. He does not take an angle. He comes in with the cargo arm hanging from his right wrist nearly to the floor, the fingertips dragging across the flagstones, a length of conduit pipe loose in the borrowed grip and a shard of glass still wedged into his left cauterizer band. Eight men in the room. Hua at the back beside the crocodile tank, and Silence on the table beside her exactly where she left it. The man closest to the door looks at Kyle's silhouette — the dragging arm, the missing hands, the shape of him — and says one word that Kyle does not catalogue. The fight starts. The cargo arm is too long for close work and too slow for fast work; it is a wrecking implement, not a sword arm. Kyle uses it as a wrecking implement: he puts the conduit pipe through the first man's sternum at a swing radius nothing in the room is built to defend against, drives the second backward into the wall by the throat and pins him there long enough to leave him. The third man fires; the round goes into the cargo arm's shoulder housing and the arm holds, the E.L.F. routing power around the failure. Kyle takes the third man with the embedded glass shard under the jaw — fast, ugly, a method he did not have an hour ago. The fourth tries to grapple Kyle inside the cargo arm's reach and Kyle puts him through the glass tank. The crocodile, suddenly free, suddenly awake, attends to the fifth man without further input. *Chekhov's Crocodile,* Kyle thinks, dry, without affect — the NeoCortex flagging the dramatic geometry the way it flags exits. *Why put a crocodile in a tank unless it is going to be used.* Six and seven go down clean. Eight runs. Kyle does not pursue. Hua is alone behind the table — Kyle has left her there on purpose. Silence is between them.
beats.location: Lotus Syndicate chamber, south tunnel arm
beats.emotional_arc: The reader feels the discipline restored under impossible constraint — the code holds even when the body practicing it is borrowed and dragging, even when the sword is not in the hand. The fight is ugly because Kyle is fighting with a body that was never his.
beats.stakes: Eight men. The cargo arm's structural integrity. The crocodile. Silence still on the table.
seeds: The crocodile released — a force the syndicate cultivated and lost control of
*Chekhov's Crocodile* — Kyle's dry NeoCortex-flagged thought as the crocodile attends to the fifth man; the only place in the chapter the narrator winks at the structure
The cargo arm's shoulder housing taking a round and holding — the E.L.F.'s power-routing engineering
Hits Kyle takes — the body is paying for the handicap
payoffs: The chum barrel placement from beat 1 — Kyle knows where to look
Hua's unaugmented hands from beat 0 — useless against him now
The shard of glass from beat 5 — used in this fight

beats.title: Eighty-Five Thousand
beats.goal: Hua does not run. She does not reach for Silence. She watches Kyle cross the room, the cargo arm dragging across the flagstones, a track of mutant blood and his own behind him. He stops on the far side of the table from her. Silence is between them, exactly arranged. He brings the cargo arm up and lays the borrowed fingers across the saya, palm down, the way a man claims a thing in front of a witness. Hua puts her own real hand on the blade above his — for one second, for the principle of it. Kyle waits. She lifts her hand. He picks Silence up with the cargo arm — clumsy, the lag visible, the E.L.F. holding the grip for him so the saya does not slip — and the second he has it the room rebalances. The hamon is cold blue, the bank empty, but the weight is right. He looks at her. He does not raise the blade. The cargo arm holds Silence at a low, formal carry — visible, present, not threatening, the threat already paid down by every man on the floor between them. He says, level: *What was the debt.* Hua opens her mouth. Closes it. Opens it again — her real hands, which she values, are visibly shaking now in a way they were not when she placed the hands of his in the chum barrel. She stutters: *Eighty — eighty-five thousand.* Kyle nods once, as if a piece of arithmetic has resolved. He says: *That's more than my life is worth. So now you owe me.* A pause. *Do you understand.* She nods. The cargo arm does not move. Then — uncharacteristic, ugly, the kind of sound a man makes when something is being taken out of him that he had not catalogued — Kyle screams: *SAY IT.* The room goes quieter than the fight made it. Hua, who has not flinched at a cleaver in this room tonight, flinches at this. She says it. Almost whimpers it: *I owe you.* Kyle does not move for one full breath. Then — discipline back in his voice now, flat, level, colder than the scream was hot — he names the terms: *I'll come to collect. One favor at a time. Until I deem we are even.* He does not say *you don't get to deem it.* He does not have to. The only mouth in the room that decides when Hua's debt ends is his. Hua nods again, smaller this time, the principle of the gesture from a minute ago entirely gone from it. Then the cargo arm lowers Silence the rest of the way and turns him toward the chum barrel. The arm reaches in and lifts out his two hands, palms up, exactly as Hua placed them. He has a length of twine he scavenged on the way up; the cargo arm loops the twine through the cauterized wrist channels with patient articulation, ties the ends together, and lowers the necklace over his head. The hands hang at the center of his chest, palms outward, dripping. He turns toward the surface without looking at Hua again. Silence is in the cargo arm's grip. Kyle has not let go of it. Hua is alive at her own table.
beats.emotional_arc: Reversal as bookkeeping — the punishment is converted into a ledger entry in the woman who issued it. The scream is the only place in the chapter where Kyle is visibly unguarded; the reader recognizes it as the cost the punishment actually extracted, and it is paid in front of the only person who could measure it.
beats.stakes: Silence. Whether Kyle kills her or converts the debt. The shape of the obligation he forces Hua to acknowledge aloud. What the scream costs him.

The Φ85,000 figure — voiced once, owed indefinitely, never receipted on paper
The scream — the first time in the chapter Kyle's discipline visibly slips, witnessed only by Hua
Hua's *I owe you*, almost whimpered — the verbal contract that makes the inversion real
Kyle's terms: *I'll come to collect. One favor at a time. Until I deem we are even.* — the debt is open-ended by Kyle's choice; the math runs on his arithmetic, not hers
The twine — scavenged on the way up, unremarkable, made load-bearing
The hands hanging palms outward — visible as Kyle walks back through the Depot
Silence in the cargo arm's grip — Kyle has it but does not yet fully *have* it (the reattachment is pending)

Hua's hand on the saya from beat 1 — countered with Kyle's borrowed hand

The chum barrel from beat 1 — emptied

beats.title: Rain, Then Anesthesia
beats.goal: Kyle climbs through the Cruciform Depot's freight grate and into the rain at street level. He is shaking now — adrenaline gone, bio-battery at 9%, the cargo arm at brownout, Silence still in its borrowed grip. The hands on the necklace knock against his sternum with each step. He walks four blocks in the rain to an AutoDoc kiosk on the corner of Ashland and Whiting — automated, no questions, accepts both Φ and biometric debt. He keys in with his chin. The kiosk reads the necklace. The AutoDoc opens. Inside, the surgical arms unfold and lift him onto the table in the gentle, indifferent way of medical machinery. They take the necklace, they take the cable-bound cargo arm, they slide Silence out of the borrowed grip and lay it on the side tray with the careful, automated reverence machines have for swords. They begin the reattachment. As the anesthesia goes in, the cargo arm's status strip — being unspooled from his stump by the AutoDoc's manipulators — pulses one last time in the not-factory pattern. A glyph forms. Three syllables in old Axiom signage. Kyle reads it as he goes under: *we are not done.* The chapter ends on the AutoDoc's status light going green, Silence on the side tray, the rain coming down outside the kiosk.
beats.location: Cruciform Depot freight grate, then AutoDoc kiosk at Ashland and Whiting, in the rain
beats.emotional_arc: Continuance, not closure — the reader leaves with Kyle still alive, the deal still active, the body about to be made whole, the obligation not yet named. Silence on the side tray is the image the chapter ends on.
beats.stakes: Kyle's hands. The reattachment. What the E.L.F.'s message means and what Kyle owes for the salvage. Silence's safety on the AutoDoc tray.
seeds: *we are not done.* — the cryptic message, the arc-target of the next chapter
The AutoDoc reading the necklace — automation accepting the ceremony without comment
The cargo arm taken by the AutoDoc — likely returned to E.L.F. salvage by manifest path
Silence on the side tray — the last image
Chen Wei-Lin's stall, four blocks away, where Kyle will wake up tomorrow afternoon eating with both hands and not saying where he was
payoffs: The cargo arm from beat 4 — released, returned to salvage
The salvage-rights glyph from beat 6 — collected on, signature delivered
Silence — held the whole way home, returned to the body that is about to be repaired

character_arcs.want: To get Silence back from Hua and his hands back on his arms.
character_arcs.need: To prove to himself that the discipline is not the hand and the blade is not what makes the man — and to find out, with no one watching, what the code does when the body practicing it has nothing left in it but a scream.
character_arcs.start_state: Bound to a chair in the Lotus Syndicate chamber, watching Hua lay her real hand on Silence's saya. Certain that the punishment is the whole of what is happening to him.
character_arcs.end_state: On an AutoDoc table in the rain, Silence on the side tray, hands about to be reattached, bound to an unsigned salvage-rights deal with an E.L.F. that has informed him *we are not done* — and holding a Φ85,000 verbal debt over a Lotus Syndicate principal he chose not to kill, on collection terms (*one favor at a time, until I deem we are even*) that put the arithmetic in his mouth alone.
character_arcs.turning_point: Beat 8 — Kyle stops at Hua's table with Silence in the cargo-arm grip, asks what the debt was, and converts the punishment into bookkeeping he forces her to say aloud. The scream is where the discipline visibly costs him; the choice to leave her alive is where it pays out.
character_arcs.cost: The hands themselves, briefly. The unaccounted obligation to the E.L.F., indefinitely. The cargo arm's status-strip glyph now resident in his sensorium as a recognizable signature he cannot un-know. The shard of cargo glass he will carry in the cauterizer band until the AutoDoc removes it. And — visible only to Hua — the moment his discipline slipped enough to scream, witnessed by the one person who could measure it.

character_arcs.want: Salvage rights — eventual recovery of the cargo arm; access to a body that can move where the E.L.F. cannot.
character_arcs.need: An asset capable of operating above the Cruciform Depot's lower levels in service of objectives the E.L.F. cannot articulate in human terms.
character_arcs.start_state: Resident in the Depot's sealed lower levels, mapping, watching, communicating with no one because no one viable has fallen into range.
character_arcs.end_state: Has made first contact with a viable surface asset, signed an unwritten deal in a single firmware glyph, and delivered a continuance message — *we are not done.*
character_arcs.turning_point: Beat 4 — choosing to extrude a control-bus wire to Kyle's exposed neural bus contact rather than letting him bleed out alongside another piece of Axiom-era hardware.
character_arcs.cost: Surface visibility. The cargo arm gone from its eighty-year position in the trench mud. Whatever the salvage-rights claim eventually requires the E.L.F. to disclose.
